caseno: Appeal from Original Order No. 356 of 1976. (with Cross Objection).
lawyer:
Sultan Ahmed, D.A.G. ------- For the Appellant. 
Abdur Rashid Gazi ------- For the Respondent.
parties:
Bangladesh  ------- Opposite party-Appellant.
Vs.
Md. Shamsul Haque and others  ------- Petitioner-Respondent.
full_judgment:
Government contested the case by filing written objection, wherein they asserted that the claim is exaggerated and inflated and the assessment made by the L.A. Collector is just and fair, and the claim of recurring compensation is very high and the respondents are not entitled to get the same. It was also asserted that the claim is barred by limitation. 

 This view has been followed in the case of Sm. Nripjit Kaur Vs. Sardar Satinder Singh AIR 1955 Punjab 190. The learned Deputy Advocate General also relied upon the case of Dasrulal Bhagchand Lal Vs. Narayan Mahadeo and others AIR 1937 Nagpur 105. In this case some of the defendants preferred the appeal without making the other defendant who was also rival claimant, a respondent at least. The left-out other defendant later on came to know of the appeal and applied to be added as one of the respondents to the appeal and accordingly he was added at his own initiative as one of the respondents to the appeal on 5-12-1934, Subsequently on 18-12-34 he filed cross-objection. Question arose whether cross-objection filed on 18-12.34 is within time. The learned Judge, held that it was within time, obviously because it may be said on the date of 5-12-34 when he was added as respondent he had notice of the date of hearing the appeal and he must file cross-objection within one month from that date 18-12-34 was very much within one month from 5-12-34. All these cases referred above are not exactly on the point before us. The point before us whether filing of the cross-objection even before the admission of appeal under Order 41, rule is C.P.C. is competent. There is no doubt that right to file cross-objection accrues fully agreeing with the above Full Bench decision of the Lahore High Court, on and from the date of hearing of the appeal or order of issuance of the notice of appeal upon the respondent. From the reading of the section it is clear that there is no prohibition to filing of cross objection before expiry of limitation of "one month" from the date of service of the notice of appeal, but the prohibition was filing of the cross-objection after the expiry of limitation. This being the position of law we may safely hold that the right to. file cross objection at least accrued on and from 4th of May, 1977 the date on which the appeal was heard and admitted under order 41, rule 11 C.P.C. if any respondent files any cross objection on or after the date of heating or admission under Order 41, rule 11C.P.C. but before expiry of one month from the date of service of appeal upon him it would definitely save the cost and the time of both the appellant and the respondent and none of them will be prejudiced in any way. 

 13. Now the question is whether the presentation of the cross-objection by the respondents on 9.3.77 even before admission of appeal would destroy the right of cross objection which could be filed even till the expiry of limitation mentioned above. The Memo, of cross-objection being in the custody of the Court on and from 9.3.77 till 4.5.77 (the date of hearing of the appeal under Order 41, rule 11 C.P.C) cannot defeat his right of cross-objection. In our view mere presentation of Memo, of cross-objection even on or before the admission of the appeal cannot take away his right of cross objection because such custody of cross objection in Court is harmless and is not violative of any provision of law. The provision of law is prohibitive so far if relate, to the presentation of the Memo, of cross objection after the expiry of limitation. In the present case no question of limitation is involved.
